Marvellously
mar'-vel-us-lī
adv. (wonderfully; in a manner exciting astonishment)
From marvel, Latin mirari, to wonder at. Three occurrences: God thunders marvellously, a king is marvellously helped, and a prophet's hearers are told to wonder marvellously at a work they will not believe.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Elihu says of the storm, “God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend” (Job 37:5). The point is not merely that God is loud but that His works exceed comprehension, and that this is a reason for worship rather than a defect in the evidence. Habakkuk carries it into history, and God says the astonishing thing Himself: “Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you” (Hab 1:5). The work was the raising up of the Chaldeans — God answering a prophet's complaint about Judah's wickedness by sending a worse nation to judge her. Paul quotes this verse at Antioch as a warning to despisers (Act 13:41). God's marvellous works are not always the ones we would have chosen. And Chronicles applies the adverb to a man, with a warning attached that has become proverbial: Uzziah built engines on the towers of Jerusalem, “And his name spread far abroad; for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong” (2Ch 26:15). Till he was strong — and the next verse says that when he was strong his heart was lifted up to his destruction, and he went into the temple to burn incense and came out a leper.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines marvellously as in a manner to excite wonder or surprise; wonderfully; strangely.

expand to see more

MARVELLOUSLY, adv. In a manner to excite wonder or surprise; wonderfully; strangely.

MARVELLOUS, a. Wonderful; strange; exciting wonder or some degree of surprise.

1. Surpassing credit; incredible.

MARVEL, n. A wonder; something that arrests the attention and causes a person to stand or gaze, or to pause.

Key Scripture

Hab 1:5 — "Behold ye among the heathen, and regard, and wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you."

Job 37:5 — "God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend."

2Ch 26:15 — "And he made in Jerusalem engines, invented by cunning men, to be on the towers and upon the bulwarks, to shoot arrows and great stones withal. And his name spread far abroad; for he was marvellously helped, till he was strong."

Modern Corruption

Divine help is read as divine approval of the helped man; Uzziah was marvellously helped till he was strong, and strength ruined him.

expand to see more

2 Chronicles 26:15 contains four of the most sobering words in the historical books: till he was strong. Uzziah was genuinely helped by God — the fortifications, the army, the engines, the wells, the wide fame were all a gift, and Scripture says so plainly. And the gift became the occasion of his ruin, because he read God's help as a verdict on himself. The pattern is common enough to be a rule: men fall not at the bottom but at the top, and the ministry, the business or the reputation that God built becomes the reason its holder thinks himself entitled to the priest's censer. He died a leper in a several house.

Habakkuk supplies the corrective to a related error — the assumption that God's marvellous works will be recognizable as good to the people they happen to. I will work a work in your days, which ye will not believe, though it be told you, and the work was Babylon. Job's Elihu says the same in the register of nature: great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend. A God whose works we could always audit would be a God our size. The believer's business is not to approve the providence but to trust the character, which is why Habakkuk ends where he does: yet I will rejoice in the LORD.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew tamah (H8539), to be astounded; pala' (H6381), to be wonderful, beyond ability; chazaq (H2388), to be or become strong.

expand to see more

Hebrew tamah (H8539) — to be amazed, astounded; Habakkuk 1:5, wonder marvellously — the verb doubled for emphasis.

Hebrew pala' (H6381) — to be extraordinary, beyond one's power; Job 37:5, and Genesis 18:14, is any thing too hard for the LORD?

Hebrew chazaq (H2388) — to be strong, to strengthen; 2 Chronicles 26:15-16, marvellously helped till he was strong, and then his heart was lifted up.

Hebrew gabahh leb — the heart lifted up; the phrase for the pride that destroyed Uzziah.

Greek thaumazo (G2296) — to marvel, to wonder; Acts 13:41, where Paul quotes Habakkuk against the despisers.

Usage

"“Wonder marvellously: for I will work a work in your days” — and it was Babylon."

"“God thundereth marvellously with his voice” — and we cannot comprehend it."

"“He was marvellously helped, till he was strong”."
